verdicts.raw:
The model is infeasible, and the cause is a structural error rather than a quirk of the problem text.

The constraint `job_assigned_once` requires each job to be assigned exactly once across all machine-position pairs. That gives 5 assignments in total. But `slot_assign` requires every one of the 20 machine-position slots (4 machines × 5 positions) to hold exactly one job. The two requirements contradict each other, so the model cannot be solved.

The problem's wording, "each job must be assigned to exactly one schedule position across all machines", is ambiguous. The intended reading is almost certainly that each job takes exactly one position on each machine, i.e. a permutation flow shop. The model's reading is wrong.

Other problems in the model:
- The start-time variables `s[j,m,k]` are indexed by position, but the precedence constraints mix job-specific processing times with position indices. For example, `machine_order` uses `s[j,mach,pos-1]` and `p[j][mach]` for the same job j, although the job in the previous position is a different job.
- The machine-order constraint is therefore wrong. It should use the processing time of the job actually sitting in the previous position.

These errors change the optimal value, and the model never reaches one anyway.
